result:
Everything passes: `bun run typecheck` is clean, `bun test` is 20/20 green (the `ValidationException` text in the output is the pre-existing PostController 422 test's expected noise), and `bunx guren check --i18n` reports full key parity across both locales.

I moved the auth copy into Guren's translation catalogs and taught the app a second locale. `lang/en/auth.json` now holds the login and register copy verbatim as it read before, `lang/ja/auth.json` mirrors it key-for-key with the Japanese strings from the request, and `lang/ja/messages.json` adds the Japanese welcome message (`:nameへようこそ！`, placeholder intact) alongside the existing `lang/en/messages.json`; `bun run codegen` regenerated `.guren/translations.gen.ts` (20 typed keys, locales `en, ja`). `src/app.ts` now declares `i18n: { supported: ['en', 'ja'] }` — English stays first so it remains both default and fallback, which is what makes a missing, English-preferring, or `fr-FR` header land on English while `ja`, `ja-JP`, and `ja-JP,ja;q=0.9,en-US;q=0.8,en;q=0.7` resolve to Japanese through the framework's `Accept-Language` detection. `resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx` and `Register.tsx` pull every label, heading, subtitle, button, and `<Head title>` through `useTranslation()`, and `LoginController.show`/`RegisterController.show` now resolve their Inertia `title` option with `this.t()` so the pre-hydration document title matches the page in either locale (it previously said "Login"/"Register" while the page's own `<Head>` said "Sign in"/"Sign up"). Forms, validation, and redirects are untouched, and the site header stays English as specified. New coverage lives in `tests/AuthLocalization.test.ts`: a catalog-parity pair asserting identical key sets and identical `:placeholder` sets across `lang/en` and `lang/ja`, plus a matrix over both pages asserting the resolved locale and browser-tab title for three Japanese headers and five English/absent/unknown ones, including that the English renders contain no Japanese at all.
